name: Pìobaireachd (Highland classical)
lineage: Highland Scottish solo bagpipe classical art-music — the highest formal genre of Great Highland Bagpipe music, distinct from light music (marches, strathspeys, reels); built around the urlar (ground), the slow-tempo composed melodic theme, and successive variations of increasing complexity through movements including siubhal (passing variation), taorluath (cumulative grace-note variation), and crunluath (the most complex variation). The 18th-century MacCrimmon family tradition (the hereditary pipers of Clan MacLeod of Skye, with the Boreraig piping college), preserved through the Piobaireachd Society codification from 1903 onward
